title: Depth Map Generation and Point Cloud Back-Projection Visualization
prompt:
Use Three.js with a 256×256 offscreen/Canvas depth buffer approach: first render a simple 3D scene (several cubes/spheres) to obtain depth values, back-project the depth into a 3D point cloud according to the camera intrinsics, and display it in the main view.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Algorithm and Visualization]
(1) The depth map resolution must be 256×256 (a WebGLRenderTarget + depthTexture or a simplified CPU raycasting implementation may be used, but the depth source must be consistent).
(2) Use the pinhole camera model: given fov and aspect, convert each pixel's depth d into a 3D point in the camera coordinate system, then transform it into world space or a unified display space.
(3) Point cloud colors: color by depth, using warmer colors for nearer points and cooler colors for farther points.

[Interaction]
(4) Slider id="fov": perspective vertical fov (degrees), with a reasonable range such as 30–90.
(5) Slider id="aspect": aspect ratio factor, such as 0.5–2.0.
(6) Slider id="pointSize": point size (PointsMaterial.size or a uniform size in a shader).
(7) Rendering mode switch id="renderMode": a <select> or button group with values 'pointcloud' | 'depth' | 'rgb' (rgb may be a colorized depth mode or a simple scene color texture mode).

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - pointCount: number (the number of points when the current mode is point cloud; in depth/other modes, it may report the last point cloud count or 0, but in point cloud mode it must equal 256×256 or the downsampled count and must be >0)
  - depthRange: { near: number, far: number }
  - fov: number
  - aspect: number (if it matches the slider, either a separate field aspectSlider may be used, or aspect may be used consistently alongside fov)
  - pointSize: number
  - renderMode: string ('pointcloud'|'depth'|'rgb')
  - cameraPos: { x: number, y: number, z: number }

Output a single HTML file.
difficulty_analysis: L5: Depth texture readback, back-projection, switching among three color rendering modes, parameter sliders, and consistency of the point count.
